cities: No store of its own in the US; a design studio and sample store in Porto · independent shops, and its own site

craft_evidence.madein: 8 of 120 style groups (7%) state a country on the product page (Portugal 3, Turkey 5). The Manufacturing page names five countries for the whole range: Sri Lanka, India, Turkey, Portugal and the UK.
craft_evidence.heritage: Brand: dated and placed (founded 2016 by brothers Mark and Chris Scholes; Brighton, now between Brighton and Porto). Knitwear partner: workshop in Istanbul working since 1989, now second generation, partnered for over a decade; the workshop is not named.
craft_evidence.process: partial: Journal says handwork, heritage machinery, GOTS organic cotton knitted and finished in-house at the workshop, with a film; product pages give gauge (3- and 5-gauge) and trims (corozo buttons); no step-by-step process page
craft_evidence.reasoning: Farafield owns no factory and names no factory or mill on any page I read. It states five making countries and says its factories are visited regularly, and it describes the Istanbul knitwear partner (since 1989, second generation, over ten years together), but without a name. That is a country stated with a described, unnamed partner, so a 2; a 3 would need a named workshop or mill. Sebastian rules.

ownership.owner: Far Afield Ltd, UK company 08090708, incorporated 31 May 2012 (third-party aggregator listing); persons with significant control listed: Mark Scholes and Thomas Anthony Wands. The brand calls itself independent and family-run.
